meta.method: Static scan (scratchpad/scan/*.mjs): data-wcs attributes parsed per binding (lhs/modifiers/path/filters), mustache + comment bindings, JS with comments stripped, markup inside template literals. Demo unit = directory with index.html (examples/ssr uses template.html); hub pages and non-state demos (signals/React/Vue/vanilla) excluded. e2e unit = __e2e__ dir or e2e/fixtures/*.html (+ companion .js). skill.count / guide.codeBlocks = fenced code blocks using the feature; mentions = regex hits over the whole text including prose.
notes: C.update is inferred (any event handler / two-way binding / state assignment); it is an engine mechanism every writing page relies on, not an opt-in feature.

C.grammar / C.state / C.bind / C.init are hit by every page that uses <wcs-state>; see detailApps for the sub-features (modifiers, mustache, dot shorthand, loading forms, $getAll/$setAll/$resolve, wildcard paths).

X.wcbindable = any data-wcs binding on a wcs-* I/O element or a user element whose class declares static wcBindable (property, spread, #init=, command./eventToken. bindings on it). `state:` on <wcs-permission> is its own wcBindable output, not a component mount.

X.component = <wcs-state bind-component> plus `state:` / `state.x:` bindings on the host element (e2e fixtures named mount-root/mount-light/mount-row are component whole-object mounts, not <wcs-state mount> volumes).

X.elemwrite counts only writes whose target is the element itself (path ending in .* / .N / .$1, $resolve(list.*,i,v), $setAll(list.*), set "list.*", two-way binding to `.` on a primitive row). Row-field writes like this[`todos.${i}.done`] are C.state (numeric-index path write).
X.i18n in demos is implicit only: locale-dependent filters (locale/date) reading config.locale, which defaults to <html lang>. No demo sets config.locale explicitly.
Filter formatting set (C.filter-format) = toFixed, locale, percent, unit, date, time, datetime, ymd, hms. In the current engine ALL built-in filters (formatting or not) ship via features/formats.

skill.count = fenced code blocks (72 total across the 4 skill files) whose code uses the feature; skill.mentions = regex hits over the whole text incl. prose and tables (the skill references document nearly every feature). inSkillMd = appears in a code block of the always-loaded SKILL.md (cheat sheet / template).
guide.codeBlocks counts BAD/GOOD snippets in 'What does not work' too.
